clues.clue: This wrought-iron lattice tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris.
clues.fact: Summer heat can make the tower grow up to about 15 centimeters taller.

clues.clue: A gift from France, this copper colossus has stood in New York Harbor since 1886.
clues.answer: What is the Statue of Liberty?
clues.fact: Its soft green color is a patina that formed as the copper skin weathered.

clues.clue: Shah Jahan commissioned this white marble mausoleum in Agra for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
clues.fact: Its marble seems to shift from rosy pink at dawn to glowing white by moonlight.

clues.clue: Carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs, this ancient city is Jordan's most famous archaeological site.
clues.fact: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean kingdom more than 2,000 years ago.

clues.clue: Built as a Hindu temple, this Cambodian complex is the largest religious monument in the world.
clues.fact: Its silhouette appears on Cambodia's national flag.

clues.clue: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type version of this machine, around 1440, transformed how books spread.
clues.fact: His famous Gutenberg Bible was printed in the 1450s.

clues.clue: Alexander Graham Bell received a U.S. patent for this device in 1876.
clues.fact: Bell's first words on it were reportedly 'Mr. Watson, come here.'

clues.clue: Alexander Fleming discovered this mold-made antibiotic in 1928 after returning from a holiday.
clues.fact: Mass production during World War II saved countless lives.

clues.clue: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flights in 1903 near this North Carolina town.
clues.fact: Orville's first flight lasted 12 seconds and covered 120 feet.

clues.clue: A unit of power honors this Scottish inventor, whose steam engine improvements fueled the Industrial Revolution.
clues.fact: His separate condenser made steam engines far more fuel-efficient.

clues.clue: In Greek myth, this winged horse sprang from the blood of the slain Gorgon Medusa.
clues.fact: Pegasus still gallops across the night sky as a constellation.

clues.clue: This Norse god of thunder wields the mighty hammer Mjolnir.
clues.fact: Thursday, 'Thor's day,' is named after him.

clues.clue: After the Trojan War, this Greek hero spent ten long years sailing home to Ithaca.
clues.fact: Homer's 'Odyssey' tells the tale of his long voyage home.

clues.clue: This Titan of Greek myth stole fire from the gods and gave it to humankind.
clues.fact: As punishment, an eagle devoured his ever-regrowing liver each day.

clues.clue: In ancient Egyptian belief, a dead person's heart was weighed against the feather of this goddess of truth.
clues.fact: A heart heavier than the feather was devoured by the beast Ammit.

clues.clue: The largest organ of the human body, it covers you from head to toe.
clues.fact: You shed tens of thousands of skin cells every minute.

clues.clue: A typical adult human skeleton contains this many bones.
clues.fact: Babies are born with roughly 270 to 300 bones, many of which later fuse.

clues.clue: The stapes, the smallest bone in the human body, is found in this part of the head.
clues.fact: The stapes is about the size of a grain of rice.

clues.clue: This butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck helps regulate metabolism.
clues.fact: It needs iodine from the diet to make its hormones.

clues.clue: The hippocampus, a brain region vital to memory, is named for this curled sea creature.
clues.fact: The name comes from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster.'

clues.clue: Leonardo da Vinci painted this enigmatically smiling portrait, now displayed at the Louvre.
clues.fact: It was stolen in 1911 and stayed missing for more than two years.

clues.clue: Vincent van Gogh painted this swirling night sky from his asylum window in Saint-Remy in 1889.
clues.fact: It now hangs at the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

clues.clue: This Spanish artist co-founded Cubism and painted the anti-war masterpiece 'Guernica' in 1937.
clues.fact: Guernica mourns the bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.

clues.clue: Hokusai's most famous woodblock print shows this towering wave curling over boats near Mount Fuji.
clues.answer: What is The Great Wave off Kanagawa?
clues.fact: It belongs to his series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji.'

clues.clue: Founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, this German school fused fine art, craft, and modern industrial design.
clues.fact: Under Nazi pressure, the school closed its doors in 1933.

final_jeopardy.clue: Dedicated around 126 AD, this Roman temple still boasts the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
final_jeopardy.fact: An open oculus at the dome's crown lets in sunlight and rain alike.
